text:
maya: Nightly e2e perf gate failed — longseq p95 jumped ~18% and throughput down ~12%. Seen on 3 consecutive runs. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/2009876543 :eyes:

e2e-ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] Nightly-e2e (longseq) • FAILED
  - p95 latency: baseline 120ms -> current 142ms (+18%)
  - throughput: baseline 2500 -> current 2200 (-12%)
  - linked artifacts: /artifacts/2009876543/

frank: Oof. Any new infra changes rolled in last 24h?

maya: Not from infra team — I checked infra changelog. We did push a runtime tweak to batching heuristics yesterday (PR #4876) — maybe that's it.

anil: Possible. Which commit/PR shipped? Can we bisect quickly? If it's batching heuristics it's probably the target.

maya: PR #4876 merged at 2009800000. I'm happy to kick off bisect but need a command.

anil: Use the nightly runner with git bisect to find the regression range. Example flow:```
git bisect start
git bisect bad origin/main@{now}
git bisect good origin/main@{2026-03-10}
# run the e2e job each step via: bazel test //e2e:longseq --config=nightly --run_under=ci_runner --test_output=errors
```

tara: Can we instead rerun the nightly with 3 repeats to rule out flakiness? If it consistently fails, then bisect.

maya: Good call. Kicking off 3x reruns now: /ci rerun nightly-e2e longseq --count=3

sre-ops: Noted. Also saw a brief queue pressure on gpu-pool-2 during the runs around 03:12 UTC — CPU steal was low but queue depth spiked. Could be noisy neighbor affecting throughput.

frank: If queue pressure correlates, reruns on a quieter pool would help. Can we pin to dedicated pool for a run?

maya: Requesting a pinned run: /ci rerun nightly-e2e longseq --count=1 --pool=dedicated-nightly

e2e-ci-bot: Rerun queued (3x on shared pool). Job IDs: 2009876544, 2009876545, 2009876546. Pinned run queued as 2009876550 on dedicated-nightly.

maya: Results: 2009876544 = fail, 2009876545 = fail, 2009876546 = fail. Pinned run 2009876550 = pass.

anil: Interesting — consistent failures on shared pool but pass on dedicated. That suggests environmental interference rather than pure code regression. Still could be sensitive heuristics.

frank: Can we repro locally with load emulation? Maybe batching heuristics behave poorly under background noise.

maya: I'll spin up a stress runner to emulate shared pool conditions and re-run the failing commit comparison.

anil: Also please collect perf profiles (pprof) and the runtime batching logs (enable LOG_BATCH_DEBUG=1). If it's batching, logs will show batch size distributions.

maya: Will do. Kicking off an instrumented run now with LOG_BATCH_DEBUG=1 and pprof collection. Job 2009876600.

sre-ops: FYI we'll throttle noisy tenants if this keeps happening. For now monitor.

maya: Debug run finished. Batch logs show average batch size collapsed from ~18 to ~6 under shared pool pressure. That increases per-token overhead. pprof attached: /artifacts/2009876600/pprof.html

anil: That aligns. PR #4876 changed the 'min_batch_fill' heuristic — it may favor early flush under tail latency, which reduces batching when queue jitter happens. We should revert the change and run the nightly again.

frank: Can we patch the heuristic to be pool-aware (use queue depth signal) instead of unconditional early flush? Longer fix, revert first.

maya: Reverting PR #4876 now (revert PR #4892). Kicking a quick smoke: /ci run nightly-e2e longseq --count=1

e2e-ci-bot: Smoke run 2009876700 - PASS

maya: Nightly rerun queued to confirm: /ci rerun nightly-e2e longseq --count=2

e2e-ci-bot: Nightly reruns 2009876710, 2009876711 — both PASS. Gate green. :tada:

anil: Nice. Let's schedule a follow-up to implement pool-aware batching heuristic and add a stress test that injects queue jitter. I'll open a tracking ticket.

maya: Thanks all. Filing the postmortem notes in the perf board and pinging owners. @sre-ops can you keep an eye on gpu-pool-2 for the next 48h?

sre-ops: Yep, will watch and alert if recurrence.

frank: Great teamwork.

maya: TL;DR — nightly failures were environmental (shared pool jitter) exposed a batching heuristic regression from PR #4876. Reverted (PR #4892) and added follow-up to make heuristic pool-aware. Gate back to green.
